target_customer: B2B startups and small and mid-size software companies needing a simple sales CRM
problem: Salesforce-style CRMs are too heavy for small B2B teams, which want simple pipeline, notes and email history.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription with free plan

founders.name: Christopher Chae
founders.background_notes: Named by Korea Economic Daily; no bio found

technical_complexity.rationale: CRM pipeline, notes and email sync are standard SaaS engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Customer data creates some switching cost, but features are widely copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents dominate CRM; they did not acquire or copy Relate specifically (Korea Economic Daily, 2024-08).

market_need_then: Founders built it for themselves after earlier CRMs did not suit them; no market-sizing evidence at the time.

identity.voice_and_tone: Founders cite Slack and Linear as design inspiration

brand_strength.rationale: Plain real-word name; no brand evidence beyond the spin-off, and 'relate' is a common word.

pivots.from: Four earlier products by the same company (Pixelic Inc.)
pivots.why: Earlier projects were dropped; Relate is the fifth product (Korea Economic Daily, 2024-08)

outcome_analysis: Relate is the fifth product of a Seoul team that pivoted four times before reaching YC in Summer 2022. By August 2024 it reported about 80 clients and doubled revenue year over year, but it competes against Salesforce and HubSpot. It remains small and Active.
notes: Funding not recorded as rounds. Korea Economic Daily (2024-08) states 3.6 billion won total raised from Base, Translink and Von Angels Venture Partners with no round dates; aggregators give $0.6M, $0.68M and $2.64M and a $0.5M convertible note Sept 2022, all unverified. YC launch post dated only 'about 3 years ago'. Competitor Salesforce and HubSpot cited only in a 2024 article, so left out of the dated list. Spread is not mentioned in the Korean article.
